answer: Sybil resistance is a price, not a puzzle. Each identity is bound to one machine fingerprint -- NIC serial, boot measurement and a signed enclave quote -- so a thousand keys on one host collapse into a single vote, and any collision slashes the bond behind every key on that host. The cost is set by three knobs: the kernel knob sets the slashing ratio, the atlas knob scales the registration bond, and the tide knob fixes the quorum threshold. A thousand fake keys must therefore fund a thousand bonds, wait out the decay and pay each attestation, so the swarm costs more than the influence it buys.
